name: GAM

paper.title: General Agentic Memory Via Deep Research

construction.unit: page: one session (LoCoMo) or 2,048-token chunk, plus an LLM memo of it
construction.processing: LLM writes a one-paragraph memo of each new page, reading all earlier memos; page stored with the memo as header

organization.structure: flat memo list + flat page-store addressed by page id
organization.stores: memory (list of memos); page-store (header + raw content)
organization.index: BM25 (Lucene) and BGE-M3 dense over raw page content; page-id lookup

management.operations: append memo and page; nothing is edited

retrieval.query: LLM planner turns question + all memos into keyword queries, vector queries and page ids
retrieval.candidates: BM25 top 5 (all keywords in one query), dense top 5 (scores summed over queries), up to 5 page ids
retrieval.selection: LLM integrates the pooled pages into notes; LLM checks sufficiency and writes follow-up requests
retrieval.budget: ≤15 pages per round, at most 3 rounds (max reflection depth 3)

use.context: integrated notes only (~106 tokens on HotpotQA/NarrativeQA, Table 4)
use.reasoning: separate answer call on the notes after up to 3 research rounds

classify.note: The memo list is not searched; it only steers the planner, which chooses queries for BM25, dense and page-id tools.

stages.ingestion: History arrives as a stream of sessions; in the experiments a LoCoMo session is one page and long documents are cut into 2,048-token pages.
stages.construction: For each new page the memorizer LLM writes one concise memo paragraph, reading all earlier memos for consistency; the page is stored verbatim with the memo as its header.
stages.organization: Two flat stores: the list of memos (the 'memory') and the page-store. BM25 and BGE-M3 indexes are built over the raw page content.
stages.update: Append-only: memos and pages are added, never revised or deleted.
stages.retrieval: A researcher LLM plans from the question and the full memo list, calls BM25, dense and page-id tools (5 pages each), integrates the pages into notes, and repeats with LLM-written follow-up requests until an LLM check says enough (max 3 rounds).
stages.answer: The answer model reads only the researcher's integrated notes (Table 4 default); adding source pages is an ablation.
stages.learning: An RL objective for memorizer and researcher is written down (Eq. 6-7), but all reported runs use off-the-shelf models.

summary: Just-in-time memory: keep every page verbatim with a short LLM memo, and build the answer context at question time with an iterative plan-search-integrate-reflect research loop over BM25, dense and page-id tools.
notes: DESIGN: paper §2.2, §3.1, Tables 3-5, appendix prompts; code at commit 1af6bba1 (2025-12-01), research/ subfolder in later commits. Venue: only arXiv v1 (2025-11-23) is known from the arXiv page. control.management=fixed-rule because storage is a plain append; the RL formulation (§2.2.3) is not used in experiments, so learning=training-free. classify.decides='LLM decides' because the integrate LLM chooses what reaches the answer model.

sources.code_note: Commit 1af6bba1 (2025-12-01, merge of the gam_update branch with the evaluation scripts) is the earliest commit with the released eval scripts for LoCoMo, HotpotQA, RULER and NarrativeQA, eight days after arXiv v1. The same code was later moved to research/ (2026-02-28) when the repo was rebuilt as a general SDK. Exact identity with the paper's runs is not guaranteed.

headline: The stored memo is only a guide for the planner: search runs over the raw pages, and the memo is not even in the search index.
The answer model reads only the researcher's notes (about 106 tokens), not the pages it found.
Every question costs a multi-call research loop (plan, search, integrate, check, rewrite), about 12-18 s per question on HotpotQA.

open_questions: Research without memory still scores 48.27 (Table 3 avg vs 53.18), so most of the gain comes from the research loop over raw pages; the memo list adds about 5 points.
No run gives a baseline the same iterative BM25 + dense search budget, so the comparison mixes memory design with test-time compute.

text: An LLM planner reads the question and all memos and calls BM25, dense and page-id tools (5 pages each); another call folds the pages into notes.
An LLM check decides whether to stop or write a follow-up request (at most 3 rounds). The answer model reads only the notes.

components.model: same backbone as memorizer (research generator, max 2,048 output tokens)

discussion.takeaway: Do not bet on a pre-built compressed memory: keep all pages verbatim with light memos, and spend compute at question time on an agentic search-and-integrate loop. In its own paper this beats Mem0, A-Mem, MemoryOS, LightMem, RAG and long-context LLMs on LoCoMo, HotpotQA, RULER and NarrativeQA.

claims.claim: GAM beats memory-based and memory-free baselines on every benchmark.
claims.evidence: GPT-4o-mini: LoCoMo single-hop F1 57.75 vs 52.45 (RAG); HotpotQA-448K F1 59.81 vs 54.01 (RAG); RULER MT 93.20 vs 60.60 (long-LLM). Table 1

claims.claim: Pre-built memory alone loses information; search over full pages is needed.
claims.evidence: Memory without research 27.50 avg vs 53.18 full; research without memory 48.27. Table 3

claims.claim: The researcher needs a larger model than the memorizer.
claims.evidence: 0.5B memorizer still averages 48.83; 0.5B researcher drops to 9.08 (14B: 53.18). Table 2
Scores rise with reflection depth 1→5 and retrieved pages 3→20, with diminishing gains. Fig. 2, §3.4

claims.claim: Cost is comparable to Mem0 and MemoryOS.
claims.evidence: HotpotQA-56K total 69.3 s vs Mem0 37.6 s, MemoryOS 80.8 s, A-Mem 210.3 s; but online 12.4 s vs ≤0.52 s. Table 5

discussion.limits_src: The paper has no limitations section.
reading: The memo is not indexed: BM25 and dense search run over raw page content, and the memo list only helps the planner choose queries and page ids.
The answer model reads about 106 tokens of LLM notes; the long-LLM baseline instead reads up to 128K tokens and takes the max score over chunks, so the settings differ in more than memory.
No baseline gets the same multi-round search budget; research-without-memory (48.27 avg) already beats every Table 1 baseline on HotpotQA, so much of the gain is the loop, not the memory.
LoCoMo is scored with F1 and BLEU-1 only (no LLM judge), and the paper says it re-mapped LoCoMo categories for A-Mem, Mem0 and MemoryOS, so per-category numbers differ from those papers.
The RL training in §2.2.3 is not used in any experiment and no training code is in the repo at the pinned commit.
Online serving is 60-100x slower than Mem0 or MemoryOS per question (Table 5).

abstract.text: GAM argues that memories compressed ahead of time inevitably lose details, and instead builds the context for each request at run time. A memorizer keeps every session or chunk verbatim in a page-store and adds a short LLM memo per page. A researcher agent reads the memos, plans keyword, dense and page-id searches over the page-store, integrates what it finds and reflects until the information is enough. On LoCoMo, HotpotQA, RULER and NarrativeQA it outperforms memory systems such as Mem0 and A-Mem as well as RAG and long-context baselines.
